title: The ordinary scalar adjunct of the continuous Koszul complex is invertible
statement: Let E and Omega be normed fields in one universe, with a continuous E-algebra inclusion h. Let p,ell,r be natural numbers, with the exact scalar restriction and ordinary action/derived invariant contexts of [lem-sfb-tame-inertia-continuous-koszul]. Let dE,dOmega be normalized all-continuous coefficient realizations and m their literal coefficient maps. For each admissible finite-dimensional representation M, the actual ordinary tensor chain map tensorMap [def-sfb-tame-inertia-scalar-mate-data], defined as the ordinary scalar-adjunction adjunct of m.koszul(M), is an isomorphism of cochain complexes. This asserts only the ordinary finite-coordinate tensor calculation, without a derived tensor, derived invariant comparison or derived mate.

source.place: Paragraph (3), extracted finite-coordinate scalar argument; steps 1-3 of lem-sfb-tame-inertia-scalar-mate-isomorphism. Agent-written calculation; Stacks 06YQ and 07A6 supply the generic derived facts.

proof.text: Choose an E-basis of N=M^H, finite dimensional since M is. For each degree a the continuous subset and basis coordinates identify the terms over E and Omega with finite free modules of the same rank. Empty coordinate sets and N=0 give zero modules.

Use ordinary finite-free scalar extension on these coordinates. Its unit is the coordinate coefficient inclusion. Its inverse sends a tuple y to the sum of y_(I,j) tensor e_(I,j). The two identities hold by balancing and basis expansion; maps are sheaf maps, without assuming sheaf-tensor sections equal tensors of sections.

The scalar adjunct is this degreewise map by its unit equation. Its source and target differentials are the same E-matrix with the same alternating signs, so its inverse commutes with differentials. The degreewise inverse is therefore a chain inverse, proving the actual tensorMap invertible, including r=0.
